questions.question: Explain the words solute, solvent, solution and soluble, using salt water as an example.
questions.expected_answer: The solute is the substance that dissolves, like salt. The solvent is the liquid it dissolves in, like water. The solution is the mixture of the two, salt water. A substance that can dissolve in a solvent, like salt in water, is soluble.

questions.question: A learner says dissolved salt has disappeared. Describe an experiment that shows she is wrong.
questions.expected_answer: Put 500 g of water on a scale, then add 20 g of salt and stir until it dissolves. The scale shows 520 g, so the salt still has mass and is still there. The water also tastes salty all through, which shows the salt is spread evenly in it.

questions.question: How can a dissolved solute be recovered? Explain how salt is made at salt pans.
questions.expected_answer: A dissolved solute cannot be filtered out, but it can be recovered by evaporating the solvent. When salt water is left in the sun or heated, the water turns to vapour and goes into the air, while the salt stays behind as crystals. At salt pans, sea water is let into wide, shallow ponds, the sun and wind evaporate the water, and the salt crust left behind is raked up.
